about: F6 odds (GAMES-V1.1-ADDENDUM §3). Inputs = ONLY what the player can see: own hole cards, the board, the number of live opponents (n, 1-7). Cards rank+suit (23456789TJQKA, cdhs); deck order index = suit*13 + rank (suits c,d,h,s; ranks 2..A). The hole and board are put in deck order first. Unseen deck D = the 52 minus hole minus board, in deck order. k = 5 - |board| cards still to come. E = C(|D|,k) * prod_{i<n} C(|D|-k-2i, 2). E <= exact_max: EXACT, every runout (k-combination of D) x every ordered tuple of opponent hands (2-combinations of what is left, opponent by opponent). Else MONTE CARLO with exactly `samples` samples: seed = FNV-1a 32 of the ASCII 'odds-v1|<hole,comma-joined>|<board,comma-joined>|<n>'; generator mulberry32 (u32 arithmetic, below). Each sample: a fresh copy of D; partial Fisher-Yates for i in 0..k+2n-1: j = i + below(|D|-i), swap d[i], d[j]; runout = d[0..k), opponent t = d[k+2t], d[k+2t+1]. below(r): lim = 2^32 - (2^32 mod r); repeat x = next() until x < lim; return x mod r. A sample: hero's best five of seven vs every opponent's (the hand-ranking vectors' key order): win = hero strictly above the best opponent; tie = equal to the best opponent; else lose. Shown: win% = label(win, samples), tie% = label(tie, samples). label: 0 -> '0%', all -> '100%', 0 < x < 0.5% -> '<1%', 99.5% <= x < 100% -> '>99%', else whole percent, half up (integers: (num*200 + den) div (2*den)). OUTS (flop and turn only, else null): every unseen card c in deck order with cat(best(hole+board+c)) > cat(best(hole+board)) AND > cat(board+c alone) (board+c with fewer than 5 cards: multiplicity categories only: quads 7, trips 3, two-pair 2, pair 1, else 0); counted under the category reached. Win/tie are outcome FREQUENCIES (how often you win outright / tie for best), not pot equity. Compute E saturating (stop once it exceeds exact_max). Apps must reproduce win, tie and samples EXACTLY (integers) and the labels. below_check: below(r) driven by an injected generator that returns `feed` in order; expect the result and how many values it consumed. made_hand: the category of the best hand in 2, 5, 6 or 7 cards (2 cards: pair or high-card). Speed: use a direct 7-card evaluator off the UI thread; the vectors check integers, never time.
mulberry32: state a (u32). next(): a = a + 0x6D2B79F5; t = a; t = (t ^ (t >>> 15)) * (t | 1); t = t ^ (t + ((t ^ (t >>> 7)) * (t | 61))); return t ^ (t >>> 14). Every + and * wraps mod 2^32, >>> is a logical shift (JS: Math.imul and >>> 0). FNV-1a 32: h = 0x811C9DC5; per byte: h ^= b; h *= 0x01000193 (mod 2^32).

below_check.why: 2^32 mod 52 = 48, so lim = 4294967248: 4294967295 is rejected, then 0 -> 0 (two values consumed); plain modulo would answer 4294967295 % 52 = 47
2^32 mod 45 = 31, lim = 4294967265: two rejections, then 91 % 45 = 1 (three values)
below(1) = 0 after one draw (2^32 mod 1 = 0, nothing rejected)

cases.why: the nut flush on the river: only a straight flush could beat it (none possible here) -> win 100% exactly
a royal flush on the board: everyone ties -> tie 100%
second pair (kings under the board ace) on the river vs 1: exact over 990 opponent hands
same spot vs 2 opponents: too many combos -> seeded Monte Carlo
nut flush draw on the turn vs 1: exact (46 rivers x 990 opponent hands = 45 540); outs: 9 hearts to a flush, 6 to a pair (3 aces, 3 fives)
open-ended straight draw: 8 outs to a straight, 6 to a pair (9s and 8s)
a set on the turn: outs to full house (K,2,9 x3 = 9) and quads (1)
overpair on a dry flop vs 1: Monte Carlo (1081 x 990 > exact_max). Outs by the rule: 2 to trips, 9 to two pair (a card pairing the board lifts the category above the board alone)
flush + open-ended straight draw: 21 by the rule (9 hearts to a flush, 6 more to a straight, 6 to a pair)
a paired board: a K or A gives two pair using a hole card -> outs; the board pair alone doesn't count as your pair
pocket aces heads-up: about 85% (Monte Carlo, 10 000 samples)
pocket aces vs 7: about a third
7-2 offsuit, a weak hand, heads-up: about a third (a high tie rate: both often play the board)
same as As Kd: the hole cards are put in deck order before seeding, so A-K in any order gives one answer
the same turn as turn-flush-draw with the board in another order: identical answer (the board is put in deck order)
